veranderings.rede: Saammeng is a compound verb in AWS spelling, so the participle is written as one word.

veranderings.voor: Om 'n vaste stof in 'n vloeistof te meng is
veranderings.na: Om 'n vaste stof in 'n vloeistof te meng, is
veranderings.rede: A comma after a long opening om...te clause that acts as the subject makes the sentence easier to read.
Totdat is the standard written conjunction; tot as a conjunction is more colloquial.
Mag for possibility copies English 'may'; Afrikaans uses kan here.
En joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma.
Dit lyk asof is the more standard written form than dit lyk of.
Totdat is the standard written conjunction; tot as a conjunction is more colloquial.

veranderings.voor: oral in die tee al sien
veranderings.na: oral in die tee, al sien
veranderings.rede: A comma before the concessive al-clause separates it clearly from the main clause.

veranderings.blok: Wat jy by 'n onoplosbare stof sien
veranderings.voor: Die water word troebel en jy kan
veranderings.na: Die water word troebel, en jy kan
veranderings.rede: En joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb, so AWS 2017 requires a comma; the protected wording stays intact.

veranderings.blok: Hoe jy die twee uitmekaar ken
veranderings.voor: Die ondersoek toets wat jy sien nadat jy
veranderings.na: In die ondersoek let jy op wat jy sien nadat jy
veranderings.rede: An investigation does not 'test what you see'; the learner observes, so the sentence reads wooden as it stands.

vlae.blok: Hoe jy die twee uitmekaar ken
vlae.teks: Die ondersoek toets wat jy sien
vlae.rede: 'Die ondersoek' is definite but no investigation is introduced earlier in the lesson; if it refers to a practical outside the text, the reference may be unclear to a learner reading the text alone. Not changed beyond the proposed wording fix, because the intended referent is content.

beskerm_bedenkings.woord: Vir oplos het jy twee stowwe nodig wat saam gemeng word
beskerm_bedenkings.rede: AWS 2017 writes the compound verb saammeng as one word, so 'saam gemeng' should be 'saamgemeng'; the protected wording keeps a spelling error, and it now differs from the proposed fix in the first block.
